profiles.summary: The endpoint still reports tempo/v1.19.1-a9d6748 on 2026-11-24, no newer release tag exists, and ruint 1.21.1 is still the newest published ruint. T14 adds one interpreter entry, the 0xef configurable account marker, which runs only when the executing code is exactly the configurable account code; the deployed PoolManager has no 0xef, 0x4f, SELFDESTRUCT or CREATE opcode outside push data.

deltas.delta: web3_clientVersion at https://rpc.mainnet.tempo.xyz returned tempo/v1.19.1-a9d6748/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu; raw tags tempo/v1.19.2, v1.19.3 and v1.20.0 return 404.

From T14 the 0xef byte executes a native shim (isValidSignature, onERC721Received, empty input returns empty success, everything else reverts) only when the running code equals CONFIGURABLE_ACCOUNT_CODE and the account has a nonzero configuration commitment; the shim writes no state and makes no calls.
A linear scan of the 24,009 byte PoolManager code read by eth_getCode on Tempo finds 40 SSTORE, 20 TLOAD, 9 TSTORE, 2 MCOPY and no 0x4f, 0xef, 0xf0, 0xf5 or 0xff in opcode position.

profiles.summary: T14 lets a configurable account send transactions although it carries code. Its msg.sender is its own address and the PoolManager callback reaches the shim, which reverts, so the state model of unlock is unchanged.

deltas.delta: From T14 the EIP-3607 sender check admits an account whose code hash equals CONFIGURABLE_ACCOUNT_CODE_HASH and whose commitment is nonzero.

profiles.summary: Scheduled for T15 (target 15 December 2026) and present in v1.19.1: a TIP-20 transfer to a zone virtual deposit address credits the zone portal and calls depositVirtual on it from inside the token. A take that names such an address debits the PoolManager exactly the amount and the caller exactly the amount; a failed zone deposit is later refunded to the PoolManager as unattributed surplus.

deltas.delta: TIP-20 transfer resolves a zone deposit address (bytes 4 to 12 equal to 0xFC) to portal_address(zone_id) from T15 and then calls the portal with originator equal to the token's msg.sender.
TIP-1094: a failed virtual deposit is refunded to the originator on Tempo after the batch settles, minus a processing fee, or parked in the portal's refund registry for the originator to claim.

profiles.summary: The zone portal becomes a contract that a TIP-20 transfer from the PoolManager can call from T15. The portal is fixed system code that derives the token from msg.sender, checks that it is an enabled TIP-20 precompile, and does not call the PoolManager.

deltas.delta: deposit_virtual refuses routing when the current frame is not the token itself, rejects zero amounts, and caps grossAmount at u128.

findings.title: From Tempo T15 a take to a zone deposit address is forwarded to a zone portal, and a failed deposit returns to the PoolManager as unattributed surplus
findings.difference: From T15, which v1.19.1 already contains and which Tempo targets for 15 December 2026, the TIP-20 precompile treats any recipient whose bytes 4 to 12 are 0xFC as a zone virtual deposit address. A transfer to it credits the zone's portal instead of the named address and then calls depositVirtual on the portal with the sender as originator. If the zone cannot deliver the deposit, the portal refunds the originator on Tempo later, minus a fee, or parks the refund for the originator to claim.
findings.mechanism: An ordinary caller inside unlock calls take(token, to, amount) with a zone deposit address as to. The PoolManager debits the caller amount of the token (PoolManager.sol:291-297) and calls token.transfer(to, amount) (Currency.sol:53-80). The token debits the PoolManager amount, credits the portal amount, and calls the portal, whose code is a fixed system runtime that does not call the PoolManager. The call returns true, so the take succeeds, and the caller must settle amount as with any other take. The PoolManager loses exactly what the caller owes. If the deposit fails in the zone (unregistered master id, unconfigured key, rejected by the sequencer or the issuer policy), the portal later transfers the net amount to the PoolManager in a separate transaction, or parks it under the PoolManager's address, which the PoolManager can never claim because it makes no arbitrary calls. A refund that arrives raises balanceOf(PoolManager) outside any sync, so no caller is credited with it (PoolManager.sol:279-288, 349-364) and it stays as surplus.
findings.impact: No funds of liquidity providers or claim holders move. The party that named the deposit address, or the router or user it acted for, loses the refund of a failed deposit, which stays in the PoolManager or in the portal's refund registry.
findings.preconditions: T15 active on mainnet with TIP-1094 in its scope (the T15 page lists only TIP-1166 so far; the code gates TIP-1094 on T15). A zone with a nonzero id below next_zone_id and a key version other than 0.
findings.mitigations: Routers and front ends should refuse take recipients whose bytes 4 to 12 are 0xFC on Tempo, or pay zone deposits from their own address so refunds return to them.

cleared.check: Opcodes in the deployed Tempo PoolManager that Tempo replaces or that T14 adds (0x4f, 0xef, SSTORE) and opcodes with special Tempo handling (CREATE, CREATE2, SELFDESTRUCT)
cleared.result: Linear disassembly of the 24,009 bytes finds no 0x4f, 0xef, 0xf0, 0xf5 or 0xff in opcode position. SSTORE is used 40 times; the Tempo SSTORE handler adds storage credits from T7 and the same cold-load rule, which earlier cycles tested through the script sets.

cleared.check: T14 configurable accounts as unlock callers, as hooks and as take recipients
cleared.result: A configurable account has the one-byte marker as code. When the PoolManager calls it (unlockCallback at PoolManager.sol:110 or a hook call at Hooks.sol:131-136), the 0xef instruction runs the shim, which answers only isValidSignature, onERC721Received and empty input and reverts otherwise. So unlock from such an account reverts and a pool naming it as hook cannot initialize. A TIP-20 take to it is an ordinary balance credit. The shim writes no state and makes no calls, so nothing reaches other users' funds. Addresses are hashes of a configuration, so one cannot be placed at an existing contract's address.

cleared.check: Whether the T15 zone portal call made inside a PoolManager transfer can re-enter the PoolManager or change the debited amount
cleared.result: The token debits the PoolManager and credits the portal before the call, passes grossAmount equal to amount (u128, which take's int128 cap always fits), and reverts the whole transfer if the portal reverts. The portal is a canonical runtime that derives the token from msg.sender and does not call the PoolManager. A revert only fails the caller's own take.

leadResults.answer: Zone deposit addresses are those with bytes 4 to 12 equal to 0xFC; any account can name one as to in take as long as the zone id is registered and the version byte is nonzero. From T15 the TIP-20 transfer debits the PoolManager amount, credits the zone portal and calls depositVirtual with the PoolManager as originator; the portal does not call back. The debit equals the caller's take, so no other user's funds move. A failed deposit is refunded to the PoolManager as unattributed surplus or parked where the PoolManager cannot claim it, which is a loss to the party that named the address only (new finding, info). T15 targets mainnet on 15 December 2026; its page lists only TIP-1166 so far.

battery.py, targeted.py and pmdiff.py were run on arc-rpc.publicnode.com (v0.8.5) and arc.drpc.org (v0.8.6): 185,529 of 185,529 vectors and 250 of 250 scripts match on each. The two locks pin the same execution crates. Which release each validator runs is not published; certificates from arc_getCertificate carry only addresses and signatures.

No public source names each validator's release. arc_getCertificate for height 32,985,088 lists validator addresses and signatures only. Every validator must run v0.8.0 or later since Zero7 and Zero8 are active, and the v0.8.0 to v0.8.4 cache fault cannot reach the PoolManager's storage (F-124). Operator level only.

Arc's crate::inspect at v0.8.6 is revm-inspector 19.0.0 inspect_instructions with the revm#3805 SELFDESTRUCT report fix and an expect in place of unwrap. The instruction loop and table are unchanged, so traces on Arc execute what block execution executes.
